scope: Proposition 4.5 (Comparison of plaque data) of the manuscript “Equidistribution of Primitive Sextic Torus Packets” (preprints/Equidistribution-of-Primitive-Sextic-Torus-Packets-October-5-2026/primitive-sextic-torus-packets.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 015 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3d96820596471fc3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the augmented limit constructed above the following assertions hold. 1. For every pattern group V , its centered probabilities in different charts agree projectively on their common plaque sheet near the sampled point. They extend to a measurable nonzero projective locally finite measure mV ω on V , with 1 ∈ supp mV ω . The chart probabilities represent its restrictions on all bounded displacement ranges contained in their plaque domains. 2. Fix b ∈ L. In every subsequential joint limit of Zi(x), Zi(xa(b))  , x ∼ µi, the two V measures are related projectively by the pushforward under v 7→ a(−b)va(b). 3. Fix a root β and an interior time scale R with room for interior depths on both sides. For every fixed C < ∞ and every sequence bi ∈ ker β, ∥bi∥ ≤ CRi, the measures mUβ in every subsequential joint limit of Zi(x), Zi(xa(bi))  agree projectively. This assertion holds for every such sequence bi; the defining grids and state construction are unchanged.
